extracted.intended_audience: program administrators, legal counsel, and participants (primary and lower tier) in FCC Covered Programs (USF, TRS, NDBEDP, formerly ACP) and other stakeholders in FCC rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and adopted rules for implementing OMB suspension/debarment Guidelines within specified FCC nonprocurement programs, covering disclosure obligations, remedies for unfavorable disclosures, delegation of authority, application to prior conduct, procedural requirements for direct final rules, and impacts on small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of substantive change for NDBEDP providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of substantive change if the disclosure bears directly on the provider's ability to meet the qualification necessary for certification as an NDBEDP provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 64 of the rules is amended to implement these disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in remedies for unfavorable disclosures (primary tier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may respond to unfavorable disclosures with a range of remedies rather than automatically resorting to suspension or debarment; contemplated responses include suspension/debarment, precluding the participant from entering into the transaction at issue, electing not to enter into covered transactions with the party for some specified period (limited denial of participation), or other less severe remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments supported tailored measures (e.g., allow entry but with closer monitoring). The Commission adopts retaining flexibility to pursue tailored measures based on unfavorable disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of unfavorable information in certification proceedings (TRS/NDBEDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may consider unfavorable information in TRS or NDBEDP certification proceedings and modify certification rules if necessary to permit such consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM requested comment on whether certification rules should be modified; the Record supports retaining flexibility to consider such unfavorable disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of alternative remedies and administrative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies may include approving the transaction only after entering into an administrative agreement (such as a compliance plan), denying the application, terminating an ongoing transaction or a specific party's participation, or referring the matter to the SDO to consider a limited denial of participation or initiate an exclusion proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant bureau or office is authorized to determine, in the first instance, what remedies are appropriate in light of an applicant's unfavorable disclosures and other circumstances. Administrators must develop and submit policies and procedures for reviewing unfavorable disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority to bureaus/offices for remedy determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority delegated to relevant bureaus/offices to determine appropriate remedies for unfavorable disclosures (e.g., CGB for TRS and NDBEDP; WCB for USF programs; joint bureaus with OMD for former ACP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated bureaus/offices will determine remedies and expect program administrators to develop policies and procedures and submit them for approval to the relevant bureaus/offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Rule 6001.345 (alternative responses to disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental Rule 6001.345 (consistent with section 180.340 of the Guidelines) is adopted to allow the Commission to address risks to program integrity without resorting to suspension and debarment action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission declines to delineate exhaustively what information warrants rejection; limiting alternative responses would risk making suspension/debarment the only option where less severe actions might be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to challenge imposition of alternative agency actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants may challenge imposition of alternative agency actions through any normal procedures currently available for seeking reconsideration or review of that type of decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies and alternative actions are subject to normal reconsideration/review mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower tier participants: same disclosure obligations as primary tier
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower tier participants are required to disclose the same information as primary tier participants; the Commission must adopt mechanisms to address unfavorable disclosures by lower tier participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPRM example: a school using an E-Rate consultant convicted of fraud in another program; additional disclosures may give agency reason to deny or closely monitor the lower tier participant and, if appropriate, initiate exclusion proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of steps for lower tier unfavorable disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant bureau or office will determine what steps to take regarding lower tier participants based on unfavorable disclosures; program administrators must develop and obtain prior bureau approval of policies and procedures governing review of such disclosures and obtain bureau approval in novel situations or when departing from those policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For TRS and NDBEDP, authority delegated to CGB; for USF, to WCB; for former ACP, joint review by WCB and CGB in consultation with OMD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower tier disclosures generally less likely to be outcome-determinative
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfavorable disclosures by lower tier participants generally should be outcome determinative even less frequently than disclosures by primary tier participants; denial of the primary tier transaction based on lower tier disclosures is not usually justified absent a 'nexus' between the conduct and the primary tier transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisionmakers may consider factors such as the number of suppliers available (e.g., limited in high-cost rural areas) when determining weight to afford an unfavorable disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted remedies for lower tier disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, program administrators may proceed with the primary transaction notwithstanding lower tier disclosures subject to targeted remedies such as heightened scrutiny, compliance audits, or a compliance plan to ensure lower tier participant does not present significant risk to program integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lower tier involvement is integral to primary tier performance (e.g., reseller dependent on lower tier for back-office functions), denial of the primary tier transaction may be appropriate along with actions against the lower tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for primary tier to address lower tier concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, the public interest is served by affording the primary tier participant an opportunity to address concerns with a lower tier participant, for example by terminating the relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggrieved participants may seek reconsideration or review through normal mechanisms if action is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of revised rules to pre-effective-date conduct (case-by-case)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not categorically prescribe whether current or new rules apply to misconduct that preceded the effective date but for which no debarment proceeding had been initiated; the SDO must evaluate on a case-by-case basis whether new rules should be applied to past conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDO should consider factors such as whether there is past egregious, well-documented misconduct and the public interest; flexible approach informed by Landgraf v. USI Film Prods. and by weighing remedial options (e.g., administrative agreements) and the remedial, non-punitive nature of suspension/debarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain separate listing of legacy suspensions/debarments and inclusion in 'excluded' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will maintain its current separate listing of suspensions and debarments imposed pursuant to legacy rules and adopt a rule construing 'excluded or exclusion' to include individuals/entities currently suspended or debarred by the Commission in addition to those on SAM.gov Exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program participants must check both the Commission's listing and SAM.gov Exclusions before entering into a covered transaction. The SDO may review existing legacy exclusions to determine whether new debarment proceedings under adopted rules should be initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclusion of excluded persons from Commission advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any persons or entities that are suspended or debarred are prohibited (during their period of exclusion) from serving on the Commission's advisory committees or comparable groups or task forces; existing members who become suspended/debarred should be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appointment of advisory committee members is discretionary with the Commission; the NPRM proposed and the Commission now adopts these prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation to implement and update adopted rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority delegated to the SDO, OGC, OMD, WCB, and CGB to develop and implement necessary procedures (e.g., public notices, templates, updates to systems of records) and to OGC (in consultation with OMD) to coordinate with other federal agencies to codify rules in the CFR and update rules via notice-and-comment where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGC and OMD may update the rules adopted, including through notice-and-comment under the APA, where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of OMB 2024 clarifying changes via direct final rule process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopts OMB's 2024 clarifying changes without prior notice and comment under the APA's 'good cause' standard but proceeds via a direct final rule process to provide expanded opportunities for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission chose direct final rule rather than simple adoption to give the public opportunity to object; the direct final rule process here is distinguishable from other Direct Final Rule processes (e.g., OFR Document Drafting Handbook).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment process and timing for direct final rule amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The item incorporating the OMB Guidelines allows comment within 30 days of publication regarding the 2024 OMB changes; until 60 days after publication, the proceeding is 'permit-but-disclose' for ex parte rules. Filings addressing the rule changes are prohibited after 60 days absent further Commission direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three amendments will become effective unless the Commission receives significant adverse comments within 30 days. OGC is delegated authority to evaluate whether comments are significant adverse comments guided by ACUS recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of 'significant adverse comment'
rubrics_metrics.description: A comment should be considered a significant adverse comment if it explains why: (a) the direct final rule would be inappropriate, including challenges to premise or approach; or (b) the direct final rule would be ineffective or unacceptable without a change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OGC concludes significant adverse comments have been filed, it will publish timely Federal Register notice announcing additional procedures. If only a subset of amendments receives such comments, OGC will publish notice limited to those amendments and adopt the versions of rules as they were at the time of the NPRM for those amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (FRFA) obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by the RFA, the Commission must include a Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis addressing the impact of the adopted rules on small entities, summarize significant issues raised by comments, and provide descriptions/estimates of the number of small entities affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRFA must describe affected small entities, projected reporting/recordkeeping/compliance requirements, and any changes made to proposed rules as a result of comments; the Report and Order provides NAICS-based tables and data to estimate affected small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary tier participant obligations regarding excluded/disqualified parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary tier participants must confirm that those with whom they do business are not already excluded or disqualified from government activities, which can be accomplished by checking SAM.gov Exclusions and the Commission's list of previously suspended or debarred entities, by a certification, or by adding transaction terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary tier participants must communicate requirements to lower tier participants by collecting certifications or including a transaction term/condition requiring compliance with subpart C of the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance disclosure requirement prior to entering covered transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with the OMB Guidelines, entities are required to make advance disclosures prior to entering into covered transactions with Federal agencies and participants in Federal programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Report and Order adopts the OMB Guidelines (with FCC modifications) and therefore requires such advance disclosures; specifics of required disclosures are governed by the adopted rules and subpart C of the Guidelines.
